column1: <"quote text" - Author | Work | Year.>
“The truth is rarely pure and never simple.” - Oscar Wilde | The Importance of Being Earnest | 1895
Price is nothing. Value is everything.
“Be yourself; everyone else is already taken.” - Oscar Wilde |
“We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars.” - Oscar Wilde | Lady Windermere's Fan |
“To live is the rarest thing in the world. Most people exist, that is all.” - Oscar Wilde |
"A cynic is a man who knows the price of everything and the value of nothing" - Oscar Wilde | Lady Windermere's Fan |
“Well done is better than well said.” - Benjamin Franklin | Poor Richard’s Almanack | 1737
“Live in the sunshine, swim the sea, drink the wild air.” - Ralph Waldo Emerson
“What you do speaks so loudly that I cannot hear what you say.” - Ralph Waldo Emerson
“Nothing great was ever achieved without enthusiasm.” - Ralph Waldo Emerson
"The greater danger for most of us lies not in setting our aim too high and falling short, but in setting our aim too low, and achieving our mark."- Michelangelo
"In theory, there is no difference between theory and practice. But in practice, there is." - Yogi Berra
“Let us never negotiate out of fear. But let us never fear to negotiate.” - John F. Kennedy | Inaugural Address | 1961
“And, when you want something, all the universe conspires in helping you to achieve it.” - Paulo Coelho | The Alchemist
“The fool doth think he is wise, but the wise man knows himself to be a fool.” - William Shakespeare | As You Like It

“Every life is in many days, day after day. We walk through ourselves, meeting robbers, ghosts, giants, old men, young men, wives, widows, brothers-in-love, but always meeting ourselves.” - James Joyce | Ulysses
“You miss 100% of the shots you don't take.” - Wayne Gretzky
"You either die a hero or live long enough to see yourself become the villain." — Harvey Dent
"Just win, baby!" - Al Davis
“Perhaps one did not want to be loved so much as to be understood.” - George Orwell | 1984
“He who dares not offend cannot be honest.” - Thomas Paine
“The most valuable of all talents is that of never using two words when one will do.” - Thomas Jefferson
“It is easier to do a job right than to explain why you didn’t.” - Martin Van Buren
"Everyone has a plan until they get punched in the mouth." - Mike Tyson
"There is only one thing in the world worse than being talked about, and that is not being talked about." - Oscar Wilde
"We are all apprentices in a craft where no one ever becomes a master." - Ernest Hemingway
"Everyone thinks of changing the world, but no one thinks of changing himself." - Leo Tolstoy
"It ain't what you don't know that gets you into trouble. It's what you know for sure that just ain't so." - Mark Twain
"The cure for anything is salt water: sweat, tears, or the sea." - Isak Dinesen
"Not everything that can be counted counts, and not everything that counts can be counted." - William Bruce Cameron
"We suffer more often in imagination than in reality." - Seneca
"It's only when the tide goes out that you learn who has been swimming naked." - Warren Buffett
"Either write something worth reading or do something worth writing." - Benjamin Franklin
"Show me the incentive and I will show you the outcome." - Charlie Munger
"The best victory is that which requires no battle." - Sun Tzu
"The medium is the message." - Marshall McLuhan
"Do what you can, with what you have, where you are." – Theodore Roosevelt
"The best way to predict your future is to create it." – Abraham Lincoln
"It does not matter how slowly you go as long as you do not stop." —Confucius
"Positive anything is better than negative nothing." —Elbert Hubbard
"Here’s to a long life and a merry one. A quick death and an easy one. A pretty girl and an honest one. A cold pint and another one!" - Irish Proverb
"May you live as long as you want, and never want as long as you live." - Irish Proverb
"I complained that I had no shoes until I met a man who had no feet." - Irish Proverb
"You’ve got to do your own growing, no matter how tall your father was." - Irish Proverb
"You'll never plough a field by turning it over in your mind." - Irish Proverb
